title: OTE Salary Meaning: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Understand OTE salary meaning and how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay. Includes casual loading, super, tax, and fortnightly estimates for 2026-27.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week and 52 weeks, the annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. For the National Minimum Wage of $26.44/hour, that's $52,265.44 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What does OTE salary meaning refer to in Australia?
faqs.a: OTE stands for ordinary time earnings. It is the amount you pay an employee for their ordinary hours of work, including commissions, shift loadings, and casual loading. OTE is used to calculate the minimum super guarantee contribution. Payments for overtime are generally not OTE unless ordinary hours are not clearly defined. For more details, see the Australian Taxation Office's list of payments that are ordinary time earnings.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect OTE and super?
faqs.a: Casual loading (typically 25% on top of the base rate) is part of ordinary time earnings. It counts as OTE for super guarantee purposes. For example, the National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05/hour (base $26.44 plus 25% loading). Super is calculated on the OTE amount including casual loading, paid on top of that gross pay.

faqs.q: Is super paid on top of my annual salary or included in the hourly rate?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary time earnings. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. For the 2026-27 year, the super rate is 12% of OTE, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. When converting hourly to annual, the super amount is additional to the gross pay shown.

bodyMarkdown:
## OTE Salary Meaning and Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you are looking at a job advertisement or negotiating a pay rise, you will often see an hourly rate or a salary figure. Understanding **OTE salary meaning** is essential because it determines both your take-home pay and the super your employer must contribute. OTE stands for ordinary time earnings – the amount you earn for your ordinary hours of work, including casual loading, commissions, and shift penalties (but not overtime if ordinary hours are clearly defined). The Australian Taxation Office provides a detailed list of what counts as OTE.

### The Basic Formula

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This calculator assumes a standard 38-hour week, which is the full-time ordinary hours under most awards and the National Employment Standards. If you work part-time or your ordinary hours are different, adjust the hours per week accordingly. The result is your gross annual pay before tax and before super.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. At 38 hours per week:
- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- Annual gross: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,265.44

These figures are from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual Loading and OTE

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a casual loading of at least 25% on top of the base rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. The casual loading is part of your OTE, so super is calculated on the loaded rate.

- Base rate: $26.44/hour
- Casual loading (25%): $6.61/hour
- Casual rate: $33.05/hour

When using the calculator, type your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the “Add 25% casual loading” box. The tool will automatically apply the loading and show the loaded rate. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor, but most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. Awards also specify penalty rates, allowances, and overtime rules. Use the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman to find the correct rate for your job classification. The pay guides include all monetary allowances and the most frequently used penalty rates.

### Super Guarantee Is Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee into your nominated fund. For the 2026-27 financial year, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings. Super is not deducted from your hourly rate; it is an additional cost to the employer. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year – super is only required on earnings up to that amount.

Using the National Minimum Wage example:
- Annual OTE: $52,265.44
- Super (12%): $6,271.85
- Total employer cost: $58,537.29

If you salary sacrifice part of your OTE into super, that sacrificed amount still counts as OTE for super guarantee purposes (unless it comes from overtime or other non-OTE payments). See the ATO’s guidance on salary sacrifice.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026-27, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide. If you have a spouse or dependants, your Medicare levy may differ.

### Fortnightly and Monthly Estimates

Knowing your fortnightly pay helps with budgeting. Multiply your weekly pay by 2:
- Weekly: hourly × 38
- Fortnightly: weekly × 2
- Monthly: annual ÷ 12 (approximate, as months vary)

Remember that if you are paid monthly, your employer may use a different divisor (e.g., 52.18 weeks per year). The calculator here uses 52 weeks for simplicity.

### Limitations of This Estimate

This conversion assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It does not account for leave loading, shift penalties, or bonuses that are not part of ordinary hours. For a more precise calculation, refer to your award or agreement and use the [reference tables](/data) on this site.

Also, the super estimate is based on OTE only. If you have overtime that is not OTE, your employer may still choose to pay super on it, but they are not required to under the Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992.

### Key Takeaways

- **OTE salary meaning** is crucial for understanding your super entitlements.
- Use the formula hourly × hours per week × 52 for annual gross.
- Casual loading (25%) is added on top of the base rate and counts as OTE.
- Super is paid on top of your OTE at 12% (2026-27), up to the maximum contribution base.
- Tax is calculated using the 2026-27 resident rates plus 2% Medicare levy.
- For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog).

This tool is an estimate. For a binding determination of your pay, consult your employer, union, or the Fair Work Ombudsman.
